source_snapshot.procedure: Stress CPU, set all fans low, reach Thermal Trip and verify shutdown/SEL, restore the fan controller, power on and verify normal operation.
source_snapshot.criteria: Shutdown at CPU Thermal Trip, correct SEL, clean power-off and normal post-recovery operation.
source_snapshot.script: No script; 50 attended and 50 machine minutes; setup requests clearing logs.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly rejects unsafe remote forcing but invents heatsink removal, which the source does not state, and overlooks a possible vendor-approved controllable validation path.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly treats the trip as destructive while retaining automatable workload/telemetry/event/post-recovery portions under human-controlled thermal and fan operations.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Thermal Trip is the terminal protection boundary, not merely a hotter version of PROCHOT throttling. The oracle is a vendor-defined shutdown transition at the mapped sensor condition, with a stricter independent abort ceiling that stops the stimulus if shutdown does not occur on time.

original_test_intent: Verify that the CPU thermal-trip protection shuts the system down at the defined condition, emits the correct BMC SEL event, and permits safe fan restoration, cooldown and normal power-on recovery.
original_method: Use only a vendor-approved bounded workload and thermal/fan stimulus on an isolated SUT, monitor independent temperature, fan, power, console and BMC evidence to the defined trip or earlier abort ceiling, confirm shutdown and SEL correlation, stop stimulus, restore cooling, cool safely and validate the recovered platform.
manual_activity: The owner/vendor supplies the trip envelope and supported stimulus; an operator controls fan/thermal actions, watches independent instruments and emergency stop, restores cooling and supervises shutdown and power-on recovery.
required_inputs: Authoritative trip sensor, threshold and event code
Maximum safe temperature and time-to-trip abort ceiling
Approved fixed workload and thermal stimulus
External temperature, fan and power instrumentation
Explicit fault-injection, shutdown and power-on approvals
safety_requirements: Use only a dedicated quiesced target
Do not remove heatsink or apply uncontrolled heat
Abort before damage if trip is late or missing
Stop workload and stimulus at shutdown
Never repeat after unsafe behavior automatically
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact trip policy and sensor mapping
Run approved bounded workload and stimulus
Collect recovered platform evidence without verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek supplies no executable test and assumes heatsink removal. Human control is required, but supported workload, telemetry, SEL collection and recovery can be automated around an approved bounded stimulus.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the model-approved CPU workload and only the validated thermal/fan stimulus while recording exact sensor, external temperature, RPM, power, shutdown and SEL state; abort at the independent ceiling, then restore and recover under operator control.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 50/50-minute scope, actual Thermal Trip shutdown, SEL, fan recovery and power-on validation remain; no unsupported physical method is inserted and logs are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record one causal timeline from workload/stimulus start through mapped sensor rise, trip indication, power transition and SEL creation, followed by cooling, fan restoration and recovered boot health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a vendor-safe stimulus, independent abort ceiling and measured shutdown/event timing while rejecting the unstated heatsink-removal assumption.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Operator observation alone cannot prove which sensor caused shutdown or whether the matching SEL arrived in the correct event window.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: If no approved platform procedure can approach the trip without uncontrolled damage risk, execution remains blocked even though the review classification is package/confirmation-gated.

project_override_considerations: The Project must provide the CPU/platform-specific trip, event and safe-abort contract. This case cannot be satisfied by the prior PROCHOT throttling stage, ordinary orderly shutdown or an unrelated power cut.
expected_evidence: Approvals, exact target and vendor trip/abort contract
Synchronized external/BMC temperature, RPM and power timeline
Observed trip and shutdown timing plus decoded SEL
Fan restore, power-on, BMC/OS/CPU/data health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require CPU Thermal Trip shutdown, event evidence and recovery. The exact stimulus and limits are omitted but can be supplied without choosing between competing source objectives.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A supported platform validation method may be available and the purpose is clear, so missing vendor inputs do not make the review globally BLOCKED. Execution stops if the only available method is uncontrolled heating or safe recovery cannot be proven.

review_improvement: Retains human thermal control while exposing automatable evidence and recovery work, and replaces an invented heatsink-removal assumption with a vendor-approved abort-bounded path.
independent_technical_reasoning: A thermal-trip test passes only if the mapped protection path causes the expected power transition before the independent damage limit. Because shutdown itself ends host telemetry, external instrumentation, BMC event timing and console/power observation must overlap the transition; post-boot logs alone can miss a late, unrelated or externally forced shutdown.
